message.content: Keep the invented workshop inventory: amber flags, teal labels, brass clips, paper boxes and wooden trays.

state.text: The invented workshop inventory begins with amber flags in a shallow wooden tray. Each flag has a plain paper sleeve and a small brass clip. The teal labels occupy a separate box so a reader can tell the two colours apart without opening a sleeve. No item in this example describes a real workshop or a stored user session. The paper boxes have square lids, and the wooden trays have rounded handles. A sample clerk places one flag beside each tray while checking the inventory, then returns it to its sleeve. The brass clips stay with their sleeves throughout the check. The teal labels are counted by row, with the left row counted before the right row. A blank card at the front of the box records that the count is complete. The card carries no name, address or account identifier. The next tray holds spare sleeves folded flat beneath another blank card. Its clips are arranged along the lower edge where they can be counted without moving the sleeves. A small cardboard divider keeps the clips away from the labels. When the count finishes, the clerk closes the paper lids and places the trays on the lower shelf. The amber flags remain in their original order. The teal labels remain in their separate box. The spare sleeves remain flat beneath their card. The divider stays in place, and every brass clip stays attached to the sleeve that held it at the start. This deliberately detailed invented inventory fits the frozen segment allowance. At the later boundary the available note allowance is smaller, so this same valid note must end the usable chain on size alone. Its source identifier, range, user horizon, writer identity, session and epoch all remain the ones recorded when the segment was prepared.
